examples.purpose: Choose accounts to link, the guide's In context, as the screen first shows it: a Card with the screen's heading in a Text, the group named by accessibilityLabel, and the Button. The screen owns each row's checked value: onValueChange stands for the screen's own wiring, which stores the new value and passes it back as checked. The screen enables the Button once something is selected; onPress stands for linking. It sets no modes.
examples.jsx:
<Card>
  <Text text="Choose accounts to link" />
  <CheckboxGroup accessibilityLabel="Accounts to link">
    <CheckboxItem checked={false} onValueChange={(checked) => {}}>Fixed deposit • 0245</CheckboxItem>
    <CheckboxItem checked={false} onValueChange={(checked) => {}}>Recurring deposit • 1182</CheckboxItem>
    <CheckboxItem checked={false} onValueChange={(checked) => {}}>Mutual fund • Equity</CheckboxItem>
    <CheckboxItem checked={false} onValueChange={(checked) => {}}>Savings account • 4821</CheckboxItem>
  </CheckboxGroup>
  <Button label="Select an account" disabled onPress={() => {}} />
</Card>

from.quote: The screen supplies the heading, owns each item’s checked state, and enables the button once something is selected.

examples.purpose: A consent row, the guide's Label with a link (the Figma composition): a Text and a Link side by side in the row's children, the Link hugging its text, and accessibilityLabel naming the row, as the guide's source sets it. onPress stands for opening the terms; checked and onValueChange stand for the screen's own wiring, as in the In context example.
examples.jsx:
<CheckboxGroup accessibilityLabel="Consent">
  <CheckboxItem checked={false} onValueChange={(checked) => {}} accessibilityLabel="I agree Terms & Conditions">
    <Text text="I agree" />
    <Link text="Terms & Conditions" autolayout="Hug" onPress={() => {}} />
  </CheckboxItem>
</CheckboxGroup>

from.quote: The Figma composition, for consent rows.

examples.purpose: Rows with an end action, the guide's With an end action: a Manage Button in each row's endSlot, a secondary action that does not toggle the row; the rows grow taller to fit it. Button / Size XS goes on the group, as the guide's own source sets it, and the group forwards it to every item and end-slot child so the Button fits the 80 px end slot (the Checkbox Item entry's rule); the Button itself takes no modes. onPress and onValueChange stand for the screen's own wiring.
examples.jsx:
<CheckboxGroup accessibilityLabel="Accounts" modes={{ 'Button / Size': 'XS' }}>
  <CheckboxItem checked={false} onValueChange={(checked) => {}} endSlot={<Button label="Manage" onPress={() => {}} />}>Fixed deposit • 0245</CheckboxItem>
  <CheckboxItem checked={false} onValueChange={(checked) => {}} endSlot={<Button label="Manage" onPress={() => {}} />}>Recurring deposit • 1182</CheckboxItem>
</CheckboxGroup>

from.quote: A secondary action that does not toggle the row.

props.name: children
props.description: Slot — a list of `CheckboxItem` (or compatible) elements to render inside the group. The `modes` prop is automatically forwarded to each child. When omitted, three default placeholder `CheckboxItem`s are rendered to mirror the Figma reference for the empty/initial state.

props.name: modes
props.description: Forwarded to every item and end-slot child. Declared: Design token modes for theming (e.g. `{ 'Color Mode': 'Light' }`).

props.name: accessibilityLabel
props.description: The group's name: on the web the group is a list named by accessibilityLabel and nothing else. Declared: Accessibility label for the surrounding group.

modes.name: Color Mode
modes.description: A token collection CheckboxGroup reads (the package's FIGMA_COMPONENT_MODES). When modes leave it unset, the resolver uses the collection's default mode.

modes.name: Context
modes.description: A token collection CheckboxGroup reads (the package's FIGMA_COMPONENT_MODES). When modes leave it unset, the resolver uses the collection's default mode.

slots.name: children
